analysis.title: Even more winning
key_insights: Brent crude fell $4.60 to $93.70/bbl, its lowest since September, after Trump said over the weekend it is 'highly unlikely' the US will order extensive strikes on Iran, assuming Iran signs a 'very strong agreement'.
Rabobank notes the definition of a 'very strong agreement' may be flexible, depending on how the Trump Administration defines 'winning' in the Middle East after losing the US midterm elections.

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie has filed articles to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth on eight counts, including starting the Iran war without congressional authorization and continuing it after Congress ordered forces removed.

Richmond Fed's Barkin (alternate voter) and Chicago Fed's Goolsbee (non-voter) cited persistent core CPI inflation, especially in services, and the case for future hikes. Rabobank describes this as a more hawkish lean across the FOMC.
The September SEP dot plot projects one more Fed hike followed by a hold through 2027, though many FOMC board members project a second hike in 2027. Fed chair Warsh's dot is missing from the plot.

The S&P 500 fell 4.4% in one day last week after the US midterms and has since risen 3%, back to pre-November 4 levels. The Nasdaq rose 5% over two sessions, led by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which gained more than 11%.
Risks to the US AI infrastructure buildout remain. The Democratic midterm win adds difficulty, and many Republican lawmakers also oppose data centres, with local moratoriums continuing to appear.

Rabobank argues the US leads in frontier models and compute while China benefits from a follower advantage and may not need to match US compute spending. The US may focus AI on white-collar productivity and China on manufacturing, which leaves the US manufacturing gap harder to close.
US Treasuries bear-flattened. The 2-year yield rose about 5bp and the 10-year about 1.6bp ahead of October US CPI.

Bloomberg-surveyed analysts forecast October US CPI at 0.3% m/m, down from 0.6% m/m, as gasoline prices fell through October from September highs. There is no y/y print because last year's October CPI was not published during the government shutdown.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down $4.60 to the lowest level since September on hopes of a US-Iran agreement.
Bloomberg survey expects cooling from 0.6% in the prior month. A hotter print would support the hawkish FOMC lean.
Prior-month figure the October forecast is compared against.

macro_indicators.reading: One more hike, then a hold through 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: Median projection. Many FOMC board members project a second hike in 2027.
Front-end yields rose while equities rallied, a bear-flattening move.
Smaller rise than the 2-year, so the curve flattened.

risk_factors: Inflation persistence, especially services core CPI, could lead the Fed to hike further.
Opposition to US data centres, including moratoriums and bipartisan resistance, threatens the AI infrastructure buildout.
The Iran agreement may fall short of what Trump called 'very strong', which could reverse the oil decline.
The post-midterm equity rebound may be fragile if the AI buildout issues are priced in later.
geopolitical: Trump said over the weekend it is 'highly unlikely' the US will order extensive strikes on Iran, assuming Iran signs a 'very strong agreement'.

Rep. Thomas Massie filed articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth, citing the Iran war launched without congressional authorization and its continuation after Congress ordered US forces removed.
US-China competition over AI, with differing paths: US frontier models and compute versus China's follower advantage and manufacturing focus.

tension_points.bull_case: The S&P 500 is back at pre-November 4 levels and the Nasdaq is up 5% in two sessions, led by semiconductors up more than 11%.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed speakers cite persistent services core inflation and support future hikes, and the dot plot shows a hike with many members projecting a second in 2027. Front-end yields rose 5bp while equities rallied.
tension_points.what_invalidates: October CPI forecast at 0.3% m/m versus 0.6% prior. A print above that would strengthen the hawkish case.
